findings.label: logic
findings.failure_mode: A Label probes table using GFM colon-alignment separator syntax (`|:---|:---|`) is not recognized as a separator row (only all-dash `---` matches), so the script treats `:---` as a real label and flags it as unknown, rejecting a fully valid pack.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:48 — prints invalid unknown-label and sets bad=1

findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: A Label probes probe cell containing a correctly GFM-escaped literal pipe (\|) still splits into an extra field under awk -F'|' (which doesn't honor backslash escaping for a single-char FS), so a properly-formatted row is flagged as having an unescaped pipe and the pack is rejected.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:42 — awk -F'|' splits on every literal '|', escaped or not
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:44 — NF != 4 treats the extra field from an escaped pipe as a malformed row
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:45 — prints invalid for a row that was correctly escaped

findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: An unclosed ```bash fence in Brief probes is never reported as unclosed because BRIEF_BLOCK's extraction awk (unlike the Wiring fence check) never resets on the next ## heading; it swallows subsequent section text into the bash -n check, and if that text happens to parse as valid bash, the malformed pack passes as valid.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:63 — awk pattern lacks /^## /{f=0} reset present in sibling checks
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:65 — bash -n runs on the over-captured block
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:66 — no error surfaces, fail() never called, script exits 0

findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: A plain URL in prose (e.g. ending in .../file.html) outside any fence is matched by the bare-citation regex and flagged as an unwrapped file citation even though it is not a repo-path citation subject to staleness checking, wrongly invalidating the pack.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:76 — regex matches the post-scheme //host/path/file.ext portion of a URL
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:77 — kept because it isn't backtick-wrapped and contains '/'
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:81 — fail() fires for the URL, exiting invalid

findings.label: duplication
findings.failure_mode: The heading-bounded row extraction for "## Label probes" and the label-cell trim (strip whitespace, strip backticks) are copy-pasted from build-artifacts.sh's own Label-probes parser into the new validator instead of being factored into one place both scripts call. The two parsers can drift.
evidence: validate-pack.sh:39-42 — retypes the identical heading-bound and trim gsub sequence as its own copy, with no shared function between the two files

findings.label: duplication
findings.failure_mode: The awk extraction that pulls the fenced bash block out of a pack's Brief probes section is copy-pasted byte-for-byte from build-artifacts.sh into the new validator instead of being shared. A change to the Brief probes fencing convention applied to one copy and not the other leaves the validator silently checking a rule that no longer matches what actually executes.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:351 — production extraction actually run by every /pr-review invocation
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:65 — the identical awk script re-typed verbatim in the new validator

the two copies have no shared source; an edit to the fencing rule in one script without the matching edit in the other makes the validator's verdict diverge from what build-artifacts.sh actually parses
